RagShortTexts: Berke's Muslim faith shaped links while his court received diverse visitors.
Religious links did not remove negotiations over passage, gifts and dynastic interests.

Variants.Content: Berke's Muslim faith shaped religious connections, while his court received envoys and merchants from different regions. Negotiations still involved status, gifts, passage and dynastic interests. Visitors often needed interpreters for etiquette and letters.

Berke's Muslim faith shaped religious connections, while his court received envoys and merchants from different regions. Negotiations still involved status, gifts, passage and dynastic interests. Visitors often needed interpreters for etiquette and letters. Escorts needed destinations, hosts and document handovers. Waiting for an audience consumed food and fodder, and changed routes could separate letters, replies and promises.

Berke's Muslim faith shaped religious connections, while his court received envoys and merchants from different regions. Negotiations still involved status, gifts, passage and dynastic interests. Visitors often needed interpreters for etiquette and letters. Hosts asked whom visitors represented, what they could authorize and how to return gifts and replies. Kin and interpreters helped, while mistranslation damaged promises and standing.
